chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ib, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the rope which is made of pig hair, by which water is drawn from the well. Can one perform wudu from that water? He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is water drawn from a well using a pig-hair rope considered pure for wudu?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a pig-hair rope used for drawing water does not render the water impure (*najis*) for ablution, establishing the principle that minor impurities do not necessarily transfer to the bulk medium. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the impurity of the object itself and its effect on the water, particularly when the impurity is not substantial enough to alter the water's properties. It reflects the scholarly consensus that *khinzir* (pig) hair is considered *najis al-ayn* but its presence in a well or bucket does not automatically contaminate the entire volume of water for ritual use.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra’ib, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the rope which happens to be from the pig, the water from the well being withdrawn by it. Can one perform Ablution (Wudhu) from that water?’ Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about a rope made of the hairs of hogs which is used to take out water from the well. Can Wudu’ be made with such water? He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
